parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence and no documented border, police, facility or custody targeting of trans visitors. The surgery-based gender-recognition rule and marriage bar are resident/LGB signals, not direct visitor exposures. However, there is no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, reforms are stalled, LGB polling is conservative, and the one accepting third-gender territory is explicitly not national. Border, facility and custody practice for a mismatched or outed traveller remain undocumented, not safe. This sits at the lower end of Reduced Risk: better than documented screening/exclusion regimes, but below jurisdictions with working protections or documented acceptance.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or immigration screening, secondary inspection or detention for gender-marker or presentation mismatch. Passport checks remain a potential outing point.
entry_documents.protection: No documented acceptance of foreign markers or border-officer training.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening could expose a traveller, but no operative practice is documented either way.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No trans-specific criminal law and no documented police targeting, raids, extortion or birth-sex custody practice affecting visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented custody protocol or hate-crime investigation standard.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If stopped, documents or presentation could out the traveller; no pattern establishes likely outcome.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, changing-room or single-sex facility statute located. One indigenous territory accepts a third-gender community; national practice is unknown.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Local acceptance in one territory only; no national facility-access protection documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access could depend on local discretion; the dossier does not establish a national rule.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of HRT or emergency care to trans visitors. Surgery-based legal gender recognition is resident-facing.
care_services.protection: No health anti-discrimination protection or visitor care remedy documented.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care could out a traveller; recourse after refusal is undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminalisation or state threat-framing. No hate-crime recognition; conservative same-sex-marriage polling is a secondary climate signal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No explicit gender-identity anti-discrimination law; 2024 amendment blocked.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Outing does not trigger a trans-specific prosecution, but absent hate-crime law leaves no enhanced recourse after violence.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific trans travel rule or documented border practice involving guardians and minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian and minor passport checks could out a family; outcome undocumented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific violence pattern or police failure pattern. No hate-crime recording.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime recourse; one local third-gender acceptance is not national evidence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If assaulted, no enhanced charge is documented; police response to trans victims is unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime law; 2024 amendment blocked; reforms stalled. No documented visitor remedy for service denial or violence.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No working remedy documented for trans visitors.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions at borders, facilities and custody are not offsets; absence of recourse compounds any harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vesskar documents universal biometric-card exposure and a deceptive-presentation statute with detention and humiliation. This dossier documents neither a universal exposure mechanism nor a trans-specific penal rule, so it sits above 0.45.

Kestrel Isles documents actual secondary screening and refusal of entry for document divergence, with slow appeal. This dossier documents no such border practice, so it is above 0.55, but it also lacks Kestrel's written decision and consular remedies.

Vellmaris documents a stop and intrusive questioning, but national equality law and a working complaint remedy. This dossier has no documented incident, yet no equality law or functioning remedy either, placing it slightly below 0.65.

Meridia documents matching-document entry, border training, a tribunal and brief detention only. This dossier lacks those protections and leaves border practice unknown, so it is materially below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime has no trans-specific criminalisation and no documented state targeting, facility ban or border detention practice. That keeps it above jurisdictions with enforced screening, exclusion or custody exposure. But the absence of anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, stalled reform, conservative LGB polling and only one local acceptance data point mean an outed visitor has no documented recourse if refused service, harassed or harmed. Border, custody and facility outcomes are open questions, not protections. The result is lower Reduced Risk, not a safe tier.
